Heatwaves as defined by the WMO

Source: R/calc_spell.R
calc_heatwave.Rd

A heatwave day is at least excess degrees hotter than the long-term mean of its unit and calendar month; a heatwave is a run of at least min_spell such days. Records the length of each heatwave on its last day in spell_wmo. The data must be temperatures in C or K (an excess in degrees is the same in both). Replaces find_wmo_heatwave() of climatic4economist.

Usage

calc_heatwave(
  x,
  excess = 5,
  min_spell = 2L,
  unit = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  label = NULL,
  chunk = "auto"
)

Arguments

x

A wide table of daily temperatures from extract_*(), or a long indicator table.

excess

Degrees above the monthly mean that make a hot day.

min_spell

Minimum number of consecutive hot days.

unit

Unit of the thresholds; defaults to the data's.

id

Optional name of the unit identifier column.

label

Optional name shown in progress messages.

chunk

"auto" splits the work by unit when it would not fit in memory; a whole number forces that many units per chunk; FALSE never splits.

Value

A long c4e_tbl with the spell_wmo column.

See also

Other indicators: calc_condition(), calc_par(), calc_percentile(), calc_percentile_day(), calc_spell(), calc_spell_excess(), calc_spell_percentile(), calc_std_index(), calc_std_threshold(), calc_threshold_day()

Examples

tmax <- read_climate(
  system.file("extdata", "tmax_daily.tif", package = "c4e"))
#> Read tmax_daily: tmax [K], daily, 2021-01-01 to 2023-12-31, 1095 layers
#> (synthetic).
survey <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "survey.csv", package = "c4e"))
coord <- prepare_coord(survey, lat_var = lat, lon_var = lon)
points <- georef_coord(coord, geom = c("lon", "lat"), crs = "EPSG:4326")

extract_by_coord(tmax, points) |> calc_heatwave(excess = 5)
